statements.text: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was going through a venue client's recent searches with a member of their team when another venue's name came up.
statements.source: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was looking through the searches with someone from the venue's team.

statements.text: Her usual position on searches like that is to leave them in.
statements.source: ev_28a85fcadf1de2f38599a19b
statements.why: Carmen said her default is to leave competitors in.

statements.text: "my default is always, like, just leave competitors in."
statements.source: ev_28a85fcadf1de2f38599a19b
statements.why: Matches the evidence word for word, with only filler dropped.

statements.text: The team member agreed, and she explained why it made sense for their venue.
statements.source: ev_760275f484a2098ab4b0dadc
statements.why: The brief says the team member explained that couples had considered the nearby venue. It does not say she agreed with Carmen's default. Her 'I think it's fine' was about a much larger venue and was given a price reason, not the stated comparison.

statements.text: Couples had considered that nearby venue as well as theirs. Those couples were comparing the two.
statements.source: Those couples could be looking at both venues.

statements.text: "Okay, good to know," Carmen said.
statements.source: ev_a824a517e71b4a8a11ad087a
statements.why: Quote matches the evidence, and the brief says Carmen acknowledged the context.

statements.text: Later in the review, a different venue came up. This time the team member placed it in a different market and didn't see its couples considering their venue at all. Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: Carmen agreed with excluding it.
statements.why: Matches the brief, and Carmen's agreement is kept as a recommendation.

statements.text: So the same review produced two venue names and two different recommendations.
statements.source: The local context supported a different recommendation within the same review.

statements.text: We bring the advertising expertise, and we take responsibility for the call.
statements.source: "I don't want to skirt around that. I want to own it"
statements.why: Matches WIA's belief statements on ownership of results.

statements.text: our Google Search Accelerator was built for: we build and launch your campaigns, and you run them with our experts beside you.
statements.source: offer_descriptors: Ads Accelerators
statements.why: Matches an approved descriptor. It does not claim this client joined an Accelerator.

statements.text: Our Google Ads lead, Carmen, was reviewing a venue client's Google Ads searches recently, and two competing venues came up with two very different answers.
statements.source: Carmen reviewed other venue names in a client's Google Ads.

statements.text: And when the first one came up, someone from the client's team agreed with her.
statements.source: The team member explained that couples had considered a nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.why: The brief has the team member supplying context, not agreeing with Carmen. It changes who did what.

statements.text: She said couples had actually considered that nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs.

statements.text: Then a different venue came up... the team member explained that one was in a different market, and she didn't see those couples considering their venue. Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: The client's team identified it as being in a separate market and didn't see its couples considering their venue as an alternative.

statements.text: So we want the data and that local knowledge in the same conversation before we make a recommendation. And then we own that recommendation.
statements.source: We weren't treating every other venue as an interchangeable competitor, and the local explanation had a place in Carmen's judgment.
statements.why: A statement of how WIA works, consistent with the beliefs.

statements.text: In a recent review, Carmen... went through those searches with a member of a venue client's team. One competing venue was a place their couples had genuinely weighed alongside them, so leaving it in made sense. Another belonged to a different market, and Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: During a venue's Google Ads review, the client's team explained why a competing venue's name made sense there.

statements.text: Our Google Ads lead found two competing venues in a client's search terms.
statements.source: Carmen reviewed other venue names in a client's Google Ads.

statements.text: Their team knew couples had weighed one of them alongside their own venue.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs.

statements.text: The other served a different market. Carmen agreed it should be excluded.
statements.source: Screen distinguishes the other market and states Carmen's agreement, not a completed exclusion.

statements.text: For another, they explained it served a different market, with couples who weren't looking at them. Carmen agreed that the second one should be excluded.
statements.source: Carmen agreed with excluding it.

statements.text: The account surfaced both names. The client's team explained how each one related to their couples, and that's what shaped two different recommendations.
statements.source: The account brought the names into the discussion; the client's team explained the relationship between those places and their couples.

statements.text: Our Google Ads lead, Carmen, was going through a venue client's search terms with a member of their team. Competing venue names kept coming up. Her usual approach with those: leave them in.
statements.source: ev_28a85fcadf1de2f38599a19b
statements.why: Matches the brief and Carmen's quote.

statements.text: When the first nearby venue came up, the team member agreed it should stay.
statements.source: The team member explained that couples had considered a nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.why: The sources do not say the team member agreed it should stay, and the evidence has no such decision. It adds a decision.

statements.text: Couples had considered that place as well as theirs. Those couples were genuinely comparing the two.
statements.source: The client's team supplied the local context: which venue had been part of couples' consideration

statements.text: Then a different venue came up. This time the team member placed it in a separate market, with couples who wouldn't be looking at their venue. Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: Later in the discussion, they identified another venue as serving a different market, without the same overlap.

statements.text: Want to keep running your own Google Ads with an expert beside you? ... We launch your campaigns, then guide you while you run them
statements.source: offer_descriptors: Ads Accelerators

statements.text: Prefer us to manage your ads for you? We do that too.
statements.source: offer_descriptors: ELEVATE
statements.why: Matches the ELEVATE done-for-you descriptor key phrases.

statements.text: They hear which other venues couples toured last month, which ones felt out of budget and which ones never made the list.
statements.source: before_publishing: do_not_claim (price comparisons)
statements.why: 'Felt out of budget' hints at price or affordability comparisons, which are kept out. The reference to tours last month also adds detail the sources do not give.

statements.text: In a recent review, a member of a venue client's team walked Carmen... through two of those names. One belonged to a nearby venue their couples had genuinely considered. The other served a different market entirely, and Carmen agreed it should be excluded.
statements.source: Carmen agreed it should be excluded.
